//: Install to /etc/host-ops-mcp/config.json, owned by the operator user,
mode 0600. The server REFUSES to start on any mode with group or other
bits set — it holds a credential verifier and every company on this box
shares the host.
bearerSha256 is the SHA-256 of the shared bearer, NOT the bearer. Generate
the pair with:
bearer=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
printf '%s' "$bearer" | sha256sum          # -> bearerSha256, here
The bearer ITSELF goes to exactly two places, and something reads it in
both:
(a) Caddy's unit environment — this is what {$HOST_OPS_MCP_BEARER} in
Caddyfile.snippet expands from:
printf 'HOST_OPS_MCP_BEARER=%s\n' "$bearer" \
| sudo tee /etc/caddy/host-ops-mcp.env >/dev/null
sudo chmod 600 /etc/caddy/host-ops-mcp.env
sudo systemctl edit caddy   # EnvironmentFile=/etc/caddy/host-ops-mcp.env
sudo systemctl restart caddy
(b) the Paperclip secret referenced by credentialRefs, for the gateway.
unset bearer
Nowhere else. A read of THIS file does not yield a usable credential: it
holds a digest.
publicKeyPath + expectedPublicKeySha256 pin the broker's response-signing
key. The PUBLIC key is a verifier, not a secret — but the pin is what
makes a swapped key file loud instead of trusted. Record the hash OUT OF
BAND at install time (the broker installer prints it); do not copy it
from a file the broker wrote on the same host without an independent
check.
brokerConfig names the OPERATOR's installed /etc/paperclip-host-ops/config.json.
It is recorded here so the install runbook can assert transport and broker
agree on the spool; it is NEVER passed to `broker.py request` (that
subcommand takes --spool only — the config is read by the host-side
run/run-once loop).
brokerEnv is an operator-owned test seam for broker.py's own hooks
(HOST_OPS_TEST_MODE, HOST_OPS_FAKE_FACTS_DIR). brokerEnv may NOT name
PATH, HOME or PAPERCLIP_DB_CTR — the server refuses to start if it does.
port 8392 is the host-ops transport. 8391 is org-request-mcp. Do not
co-locate them: one port per transport, so a firewall rule or a Caddy
matcher can name exactly one principal class.
